quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: You can drive in a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane if:

options.text: You are driving faster than other traffic.
You are driving slower than other traffic.
Your vehicle has more than one person in it.
You need to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has more than one person in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways have special left lanes for vehicles with multiple people. These HOV lanes are marked with signs and diamond shapes on the road.

questions.question: Which drugs can make you a less safe driver?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make you a worse driver. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is against the law.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction the chevron points. In this case, the road curves left. You may see several of these signs placed along the curve.

questions.question: After a train passes a railroad crossing where you stopped, you should:

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move forward until all gates are fully raised and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: You cannot make a U-turn:

options.text: If it requires crossing a double yellow line.
If it will get in the way of other traffic.
Near hills, curves, or poor visibility.

questions.explanation: Before making a U-turn, make sure it is allowed. Check for hills, curves, signs that ban U-turns, double yellow lines, other traffic, and visibility.

questions.question: In a car on a highway, it is:

options.text: Illegal to drink alcohol or have an open bottle in the car.
Legal to drink alcohol if you are not the driver.
Legal to drink alcohol if you are driving but not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal to drink alcohol or have an open bottle in the car.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive while drunk. No one in the car—including passengers—can drink alcohol or have an open bottle of alcohol when the car is running.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Slow down to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before you enter a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking while turning can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: At a four-way stop sign:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to arrive at the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: You can drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving:

options.text: If the train is not too close.
If your car does not hit the gate.
If you look both ways first.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: You can drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a person signaling, or a train horn. Never try to drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you need more strength to steer. Slow down and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve signals and body functions. It lowers inhibitions and hurts your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speed increases the risk of death in a crash.
Higher speed means you need more following distance.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Faster speeds need longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance as you go faster.

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: To merge safely, find a gap large enough for your vehicle. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to enter.

questions.question: When passing, when can you return to your lane safely?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you are far enough from the other vehicle. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let any traffic or pedestrians still in the intersection pass.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another vehicle passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let the passing vehicle return to your lane easily.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for traffic to pass. You can enter the intersection if the light is green and no vehicle ahead is turning left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: Water on the road causes hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when standing water is on the road. Below 35 mph, most tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water fast enough. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on the water.

questions.question: A traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will soon turn red. Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes if your vehicle skids. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors—they do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and road. Low air pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases risk.

questions.question: Driving is a privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. A driver's license means you have a serious responsibility to keep yourself and others safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Watch carefully for workers and equipment in the area.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell drivers about hazardous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible dangers. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them could cause an accident.
